messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 | OmniHealth (Private VPC, dedicated pool dp-07) — 30% of requests returning 502/504 from private endpoints in us-west-2. Alert: https://grafana.redwood/alerts/2345 — paging oncall.

oncall-ash: acknowledging, I'm on it. Paging SRE. Can someone grab customer contact and recent deploys?

sre_jamie: looking at logs now — spikes started at 2026-02-28T03:12:xxZ. Error pattern: TCP RST between NLB and backend nodes, health checks toggling. Only affects dp-07 (OmniHealth). Not seeing control plane errors.

kevin-cs: looped in {customer-ops-omni} — their support alias: ops@omnihealth.internal. They confirm impact for production traffic to model endpoints.

eng-runtime-raj: copying logs from runtime: 
```
2026-02-28T03:13:02Z WARN upstream connection reset by peer target=i-0f123... node=dp-07-rt-2
2026-02-28T03:13:05Z INFO healthcheck failed port=8080 target=i-0f123...
```
Potential mismatch between NLB healthcheck port/path and process.

infra-alex: quick context: OmniHealth uses an internal NLB in front of instances (tls passthrough), Route53 private zone pointing to NLB static IPs, and customer-managed security groups. We recently pushed a template that suggests using port 8080 for runtime, but customer's infra might still be on 8443 or 443.

oncall-ash: can someone confirm current NLB health check config (port/protocol)? If it's wrong we can reconfigure or re-register targets as a temporary mitigation.

eng-runtime-raj: grabbing NLB config via account runbook (customer-managed infra) — they shared these ARNs earlier. From their export: 
```
HealthCheckProtocol: TCP
HealthCheckPort: 8443
TargetGroupPort: 8080
```
So NLB is probing 8443 -> targets listening 8080. That's a mismatch. If NLB does TCP probe to 8443 but instance resets because nothing listening on 8443 -> unhealthy.

infra-alex: that explains repeated RSTs in logs. Two ways to mitigate quickly: (1) change target group/healthcheck to port 8080 (preferred), or (2) open a small port-forward on the node so 8443 -> 8080 locally until config can be harmonized. Which can customer do quickly?

customer-ops-omni: ops@omni: we just rolled a hardening patch that closed 8443 accidentally in SG. We can flip SG but need your exact CIDR for NLB healthchecks and an approved change window (this is prod). ETA ~10min if approved.

kevin-cs: we can authorize now, customer provided change window in thread. Alex, what SG rule do they need to add?

infra-alex: they should add an ingress rule to their instance SG allowing the NLB's healthcheck source. For NLB internal, source will be the NLB nodes' private IPs — AWS recommends allowing the NLB security group or the NLB nodes via prefix list. Example command they can run: 
```
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0abcd1234 --protocol tcp --port 8443 --cidr 10.0.0.0/22
```
But safer: allow from the NLB's SG (if they use one): 
```
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0abcd1234 --protocol tcp --port 8443 --source-group sg-0nlb12345
```
Add only for the duration of the incident.

oncall-ash: kevin, tell them to add the SG rule and confirm. While they do that, can eng-runtime-raj try a local workaround on dp-07 nodes to accept 8443 and proxy to 8080 (socat/nc)?

eng-runtime-raj: I can push a one-off fix via our bootstrap script that runs in the node agent (we have access via customer-approved runbook). Command I'd run (on each node): 
```
sudo apt-get install -y socat
sudo systemd-run --unit=socat-8443 -p Type=simple -- /usr/bin/socat TCP-LISTEN:8443,reuseaddr,fork TCP:127.0.0.1:8080
```
This will accept 8443 and forward to 8080. It is ephemeral and easy to undo. Need approval from customer.

customer-ops-omni: approved for emergency change. Please proceed and we'll update SG immediately.

oncall-ash: go for it Raj. Alex coordinate with customer on SG. Kevin, keep legal/compliance in the loop if needed.

eng-runtime-raj: deploying socat proxy to dp-07 nodes now. Running on dp-07-rt-{1,2,3}. Confirming process started on all three.

infra-alex: customer confirms SG rule added (ingress tcp 8443 from sg-0nlb12345). Health checks immediately went healthy.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Alert update: healthcheck failures reduced to 0, error rate back to baseline. Time to mitigate: ~8 minutes.

kevin-cs: I just spoke to customer PM; they reported brief user-facing failures for ~7 minutes. They're ok with mitigation. We'll coordinate a rolling fix for matching ports and update their IaC template.

eng-runtime-raj: next steps I propose: (1) schedule a config sync — change target group healthcheck to 8080 or switch runtime to listen on 8443 consistently, (2) remove temporary socat and revert SG change after long-term fix is in place, (3) postmortem documenting root cause (customer SG hardening + mismatch with our recommended port).

oncall-ash: handing off to weekend oncall @sre_lin for follow-ups and postmortem. Summary to include: customer=OmniHealth, deployment=Private VPC dp-07 us-west-2, root cause=SG hardening closed healthcheck port + mismatch between NLB healthcheck (8443) and target port (8080), mitigation=customer added SG rule and we deployed transient socat proxy.

sre_lin: ack'd — will pick up tomorrow, will create tracking ticket, and I'll coordinate with Solutions to update the runbook and IaC snippets.

kevin-cs: closing customer loop now. Thanks everyone. Postmortem owner: @sre_lin.

incident-bot: INCIDENT REPORTED -> MITIGATED | P1 resolved (candidate) at 2026-02-28T03:20:59Z.
